head.h1: Corporate Event Catering in Dubai — What It Costs and How to Book

opening_paragraph: Corporate event catering in Dubai from myCHEF starts at AED 700 per person , with a vetted chef and full-service team running your gala, launch or conference so guests remember the evening and not the logistics. It is the big set-piece night handled properly — menu, service, setup and cleanup carried by people who do this every week — priced to your headcount instead of a fixed package you have to squeeze your event into. Tell us the date, the numbers and the room, and during our published business hours you will have an itemised proposal back promptly.

new_paragraphs: It includes everything between the brief and the last cleared plate: a tailored corporate event menu, a matched chef and service team, on-site cooking or delivery, full setup, and cleanup afterwards. A good corporate event caterer in Dubai does not just drop food — they read the room. For a 200-guest gala that means timed courses that land while speeches run to schedule; for a launch it means canapés that circulate without stalling the networking. Our corporate event catering services in Dubai cover front-of-house staffing, glassware and equipment, dietary handling across the guest list, and a single point of contact from quote to wrap. As a corporate event catering company, myCHEF treats the food as one moving part of a larger evening you are responsible for delivering to leadership, clients or the board.

replace_in_block.new_heading: What goes on a corporate event menu in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A corporate event menu in Dubai is built around your format, your guest mix and the Dubai audience. Plated dinners typically run three or four courses; receptions run canapés and grazing; conferences run buffets and working-lunch platters. Because Dubai guest lists are international, every corporate event food catering plan is fully halal by default and layers in vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and nut-free options without a separate "special" table that singles people out. A private corporate event chef designs the menu with you instead of handing over a fixed card — seasonal produce, cuisine you want, and dishes that plate and travel well at scale. Cuisines range from modern European and Mediterranean to Arabic, Indian and pan-Asian, and can be themed to a brand, a season or a launch. We confirm the final corporate event menu in Dubai at tasting or sign-off before the date.
How much does corporate event catering cost in Dubai?

It starts from around AED 700 per person and is quoted by headcount, menu and service level. Package tiers run from AED 1,200 to 5,500 depending on courses and staffing, and regular or retained arrangements can be priced per programme.
What's included in the service?
Included is menu design, a vetted chef, front-of-house service or delivery, full setup, and cleanup where relevant — so your team runs the event instead of the buffet.
Do you cater large conferences and galas?
Yes. We scale corporate event catering for events from a 20-seat board dinner to a 500-guest conference or gala, plated or on live stations, run to your agenda.
Can the corporate event menu be customised?

Yes. A private corporate event chef builds the corporate event menu with you — cuisine, courses and format — and it is fully halal by default with vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and nut-free options handled across the guest list.
How do I hire or set up a regular arrangement?

Tell us your needs, headcount and schedule; we send an itemised proposal, promptly during our published business hours, and can set up an ongoing arrangement with consistent menus and simplified billing.
Is there affordable and luxury corporate event catering?
Yes to both. We offer affordable corporate event catering for routine functions and luxury corporate event catering for flagship evenings — the cost tracks the format and service you choose.
Do you cover my area of Dubai?
We deliver corporate event catering across all of Dubai, including DIFC, Business Bay, Downtown, Palm Jumeirah and the main exhibition venues, bringing the chef and team to your venue or office.
How much will it cost to feed 40 guests?

Work it as a per-head sum: 40 guests at the AED 700 starting figure gives you the food and service line, and 5% VAT goes on top of it. Format moves that total more than anything else — a drop-off or buffet for 40 sits at the bottom of the range, a plated dinner with three or more service staff sits at the top, and live stations land in between. Two other numbers matter at that size: myCHEF works to a minimum of 10 guests on volume formats and 20 on a buffet, both comfortably below 40, and a minimum order value of AED 900. The proposal itemises food, staffing and equipment separately, so you can see which of the three is driving the figure.
Do you cater small corporate events?

Yes. Small corporate event catering in Dubai — a ten-seat board dinner, a client lunch for six on a plated menu, a small party for a team that has just shipped something — is a normal part of the week, not an exception we squeeze in. Volume formats start at 10 guests, with 20 for a full buffet spread, and there is a minimum order value of AED 900; a chef cooking a plated menu carries no headcount minimum, so a board table of six works the same way as a table of sixteen.
What is the leading catering company in Dubai?

Nobody leads it outright. Dubai's catering market is split across hotel banqueting teams, large volume caterers, chef-led boutique outfits and delivery kitchens, and the supplier that suits a 300-guest gala is seldom the one that suits a 12-person board dinner. So judge a shortlist on four checkable things: whether per-head prices are published or only quoted on request, who does the cooking and whether you learn their name before the day, whether the quote is itemised line by line, and who is accountable on the night if something slips. MyCHEF publishes its per-head figure and its package tiers on this page for that reason. The best corporate event catering in Dubai is, in practice, the supplier that answers those four questions plainly.
For corporate event catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .

We provide corporate event catering across the whole of Dubai, from DIFC, Business Bay and Downtown boardrooms to Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Marina, JLT and the exhibition venues around Trade Centre and Expo City. Wherever your function sits, we bring the chef, team and kit to you — this is corporate event home catering and in-office catering as readily as ballroom service. add_block.new_heading: What belongs on a corporate checklist Dubai teams trust?
new_paragraphs: Start with the numbers and the non-negotiables. A dependable checklist covers headcount, dietary and religious requirements, allergies, the date, the venue and a per-head budget before a single menu is discussed. For a mixed office, make vegetarian, halal and nut-aware options standard instead of afterthoughts, so no colleague is left with a side salad. Add the practical layer next: parking and loading access, a booked service lift, power for hot-holding, and a clear pack-down time. Write it as a living document you reuse for every event; that repetition is what turns a scramble into a routine. If you take one idea from this guide, make it this: the brief you write is the meal you get, so vague inputs produce vague catering. Good caterers work happily from a tight checklist and will flag anything you have missed.

add_block.new_heading: Do corporate caterers in Dubai need a food safety licence?
new_paragraphs: Yes, and this is the first thing to verify. Any business that prepares or serves food in Dubai operates under the Dubai Municipality Food Code, and one rule matters most when you vet a caterer: every food business must have at least one trained, certified Person In Charge (PIC) responsible for daily food-safety compliance, supported by a HACCP-based system. According to the Dubai Municipality Food Code , this is a baseline expectation, not a premium extra. When you shortlist suppliers, ask to see the trade licence, the food-preparation permit for their kitchen, and evidence of PIC training. A caterer who answers these questions comfortably is telling you they run a real, inspected operation instead of an unlicensed home setup. This single check filters out most of the risk before you taste a thing.

add_block.new_heading: How is the food kept safe on the way to your office?
new_paragraphs: Through strict temperature control in transit, which is worth confirming for any drop-off order. Dubai Municipality's food-transport guidance sets clear thresholds: hot food held at 60°C or above, cold food at 5°C or below, with hot and cold items segregated in separate insulated units. Per the Dubai Municipality transport guideline , vehicles carrying prepared food must be equipped to maintain those temperatures. For an office lunch that sits out during a long meeting, ask how the caterer holds temperature on site, not just in the van. Chafing fuel, insulated boxes and a realistic serving window keep a working lunch safe and appetising instead of lukewarm by the second agenda item. It is a fair question to put to any supplier, and a good one to answer.

add_block.new_heading: How much does corporate catering cost per head in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Expect a floor around AED 700 per person for clear office catering, rising with format and staffing. A simple drop-off working lunch sits at the lower end; plated client dinners and award nights with on-site chefs and service staff cost significantly more per head. Two drivers move the number most: how many staff you need in the room, and how many courses leave the kitchen. Remember that catering in the UAE carries VAT at the standard 5% rate confirmed by the UAE Ministry of Finance , so ask whether quoted prices are inclusive. The best value rarely means the lowest headline figure; it means a clear, itemised proposal where you can compare prices and see exactly what each dirham buys.

add_block.new_heading: How do you time catering around the Dubai working day?
new_paragraphs: Anchor the menu to the office clock. The UAE private-sector standard is eight working hours a day and 48 a week, typically Monday to Friday, as set out by the UAE Government under Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021. That rhythm shapes service windows: arrival coffee before the first session, a working lunch that does not overrun the agenda, and an afternoon pick-me-up. Agree exact drop and serve times, confirm building access and a service lift, and give the caterer a pack-down slot that clears before the next meeting. Dubai's calendar is busy — Dubai World Trade Centre alone welcomed 2.65 million event participants across 2024 — so book popular dates early. Precise timing is what separates a smooth boardroom lunch from a cold one.

add_block.new_heading: One-off event or recurring office catering?
new_paragraphs: Decide this before you brief, because it changes the whole planning approach. For a single gala or town hall, a fixed package keeps costs predictable and the menu tight. If you feed the team weekly, a retainer with rotating menu ideas gives consistency, simpler monthly billing and a caterer who already knows your dietary map. Either way, insist on an itemised proposal so recurring services do not quietly drift upward. This is also where you standardise the boring-but-vital details: invoicing terms, a named contact, substitution rules and a cut-off for final numbers. Teams that search for "corporate catering near me" often stop at the first result; a short, structured comparison of two or three suppliers against the same brief consistently produces better food and fairer quotes. Treat the checklist as your procurement tool, not a menu wish-list.
